title.en: C Review: Pointers, Structs and malloc
title.bn: সি ঝালাই: পয়েন্টার, struct ও malloc

summary.en: Follow node addresses, change a caller’s head and release allocated storage safely.
summary.bn: নোডের অ্যাড্রেস ধরো, ফাংশন থেকে head বদলাও, আর বরাদ্দ করা মেমরি ছেড়ে দাও।

notes: These implementations use C17. Compound literals and declarations in loop headers date from C99; C17 does not add automatic memory management.

examples.title: Change a node through a pointer
examples.explanationHtml: cur points at node, so cur->value changes the original object. The pointer itself holds no separate copy of the mark.

examples.title: Allocate, use and release one node
examples.explanationHtml: malloc reserves room for the complete Node. Clearing this owner after free helps avoid accidental reuse, but other aliases would still need care.

examples.title: Replace the caller’s head
examples.explanationHtml: The function receives &head. Writing *head changes the caller’s pointer, so the second node becomes the new first node.

practice.title: Update through an address
practice.statementHtml: Read one integer (-99..99). Use a pointer parameter to add five; print Value: and the new number.
hints: Dereference the parameter to change the caller’s object.

practice.title: Prepend through the head address
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16), n values (-99..99), then one new value (-99..99). Print List: followed by the updated chain.
hints: Pass &head so the function can replace head.

practice.title: Copy values into independent storage
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16) and n values (-99..99). Allocate a copy, increase its first value if present, then print original Values: and copied Values:.
hints: Copy elements, since copying a pointer would still share storage.

practice.title: Clear a chain through its owner
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16) and n values (-99..99). A function must release all nodes and set the caller’s head to NULL. Print Cleared: 1.
hints: Save next before free, then clear the external owner.

quiz.prompt: For Node *cur, what does cur->value mean?
options: A copy of the whole list
quiz.explanation: The arrow first dereferences cur and then selects the member; cur must point to a valid Node.

quiz.prompt: Why allocate malloc(sizeof *node) rather than sizeof node?
options: A pointer always occupies zero bytes
The node object can be larger than its pointer
quiz.explanation: sizeof node measures the pointer. malloc does not initialize the newly allocated Node.

quiz.prompt: Which argument allows prepend to replace head in its caller?
quiz.explanation: The address of the pointer has type Node **. Assignment through it changes the caller’s head.

quiz.prompt: What must you check before dereferencing malloc’s result?
options: Whether the address prints as an even number
Whether the node value is positive
quiz.explanation: Allocation can fail. Dereferencing NULL has undefined behavior.

quiz.prompt: After free(node), which operation is valid?
options: Assign NULL to the pointer variable
quiz.explanation: The pointer variable still exists, but the freed object does not. Clearing the owner does not clear aliases.

quiz.prompt: Which member type allows a node to refer to its own structure type?
quiz.explanation: A pointer has a known size even before the complete Node layout is finished. Embedding a full Node recursively would require infinite size.

quiz.prompt: Why does a local copy of head fail to update the caller after assignment?
options: C passes the pointer value by value
quiz.explanation: Changing a local pointer changes only that local object. Return the new pointer or pass its address.

quiz.prompt: When a pointer increments the stored mark, which value changes?
quiz.explanation: cur identifies mark, so *cur += 5 changes the same object from 72 to 77.

quiz.prompt: What remains after changing only a local pointer copy?
quiz.explanation: Reassigning copy changes only that pointer. head still identifies first=12, while copy identifies second=24.

quiz.prompt: Which member does the arrow assignment update?
quiz.explanation: cur points at node. The arrow assignment replaces node.value with 91, which the final print reads.

keyPoints.en: A pointer stores an address rather than the pointed-to value.
keyPoints.bn: পয়েন্টারে মানের বদলে সেই মানের অ্যাড্রেস থাকে।

keyPoints.en: The arrow operator accesses a structure member through a pointer.
keyPoints.bn: পয়েন্টার দিয়ে struct-এর সদস্য ধরতে arrow অপারেটর ব্যবহার করো।

keyPoints.en: Allocate sizeof *node so the requested space matches the node type.
keyPoints.bn: নোডের টাইপের সঙ্গে বরাদ্দ মেলাতে sizeof *node ব্যবহার করো।

keyPoints.en: A pointer-to-pointer lets a function replace the caller’s pointer.
keyPoints.bn: পয়েন্টারের পয়েন্টার দিলে ফাংশন কলারের পয়েন্টার বদলাতে পারে।

keyPoints.en: Save a node’s successor before releasing that node.
keyPoints.bn: নোড free করার আগে তার পরের নোডের অ্যাড্রেস রেখে দাও।

examQuestions.question: Explain Node * and Node ** using insertion at head.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Node * identifies a node. Node ** identifies a pointer field, such as the caller’s head. A prepend function can link the new node to *head and then assign *head = node.

examQuestions.question: Write the core steps of allocating a node and prepending it, with failure handling.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
Node *node = malloc(sizeof *node);
if (node == NULL) {
    return 0;
}
node->value = value;
node->next = *head;
*head = node;
return 1;

examQuestions.question: Explain why free(head); head = head->next; is unsafe and repair it.
examQuestions.answerHtml: free ends the node’s lifetime, so reading head->next afterward accesses freed storage. First save Node *next = head->next; then free(head); then assign head = next. Repeat until NULL and clear the external head when finished.
